stack_detection.method: UIA probe with latch protocol (probe -> poke -> re-probe)
stack_detection.signature: first UIA walk returns 257 nodes of browser chrome WITHOUT page content (the stub); the walk itself is the assistive-client signal — 328 nodes WITH full page content by the second walk, t+1.4 s. No --force-renderer-accessibility needed

channel_setup: UI Automation via Python `uiautomation` against a normally-launched Chrome (no accessibility flags). Chromium enables renderer accessibility on detecting the UIA client (WM_GETOBJECT traffic).

t1_read_text.detail: After the latch: full page text ('Dupont SARL', '3 open orders' …) plus browser chrome the CDP channel cannot see (tabs, toolbar, status bubble).

t2_enumerate.detail: 37 interactive lines = page's 10 + browser chrome (tab strip, toolbar, bookmarks bar). Frames are physical screen pixels, directly clickable — no CSS-frame conversion needed (the macOS DPR trap does not exist via UIA).

t3_live_value.detail: Focused the field via UIA, typed; value="UIA-DUAL-42q" visible in the re-walked view. Diff 975 B (UIA diffs are heavier than CDP's 56 B for the same edit — coarser tree granularity).

t4_living_screen.detail: Living screen measured on the CDP twin cell (120-239 B/tick); not repeated here.

t5_blind_action.detail: Blind click already proven both via CDP (same page) and via UIA (Calculator/Explorer); not repeated.

t6_pictorial.detail: allcanvas.html via UIA: document node + '[pixels] image 48,127,1280,800' — the canvas declared with its exact rect, zero fabricated text inside it. (One text line below the content area is Chrome's own 'fichier local ou partagé' status bubble — really on screen, correctly reported.)

measurements.notes: THE WINDOWS AT-LATCH, quantified: stub (257 nodes, no content) -> latched (328 nodes, full content) in ONE extra walk ~1.2 s later; faster and more automatic than macOS (no AXEnhancedUserInterface incantation, no error codes — the UIA query IS the trigger). Channel comparison on the identical screen: UIA 969 tok / ~200 ms vs CDP 273 tok / 8 ms (3.5x lighter, 25x faster) — but UIA sees browser chrome and speaks screen-global coordinates. Same pairing conclusion as macOS: CDP for the page, accessibility for the window; a router should hold both. Router rule confirmed for Windows: NEVER classify a Chromium app from the first UIA read.
